captive_summary: A real 6.6 MW (2x3.3 MW) gas-engine power plant (PLTMG) has operated at Teluk Lamong Port since Jan 2018, but it is documented as powering PT Terminal Teluk Lamong / the Kawasan Pelabuhan Teluk Lamong -- the Pelindo container/multipurpose terminal company -- not the still-under-construction PGN small-scale LNG import facility that is the GEM record's subject. This is a 'captive to whom' case: the plant belongs to a different industrial host at the same port location.
confirmed_how: Multiple Indonesian outlets (Bisnis.com, Kontan, Antara Jatim) report PT Widar Mandripa Nusantara (a PGN subsidiary/JV) operating a 2x3.3 MW PLTMG since Jan 2018 that supplies electricity to 'PT Terminal Teluk Lamong' / 'Kawasan Pelabuhan Teluk Lamong.' 'PT Terminal Teluk Lamong' is the Pelindo-affiliated container/multipurpose terminal operating company (opened 2014), a separate facility and separate corporate tenant from the LNG import terminal that is the GEM record's subject (PGN's small-scale LNG receiving facility, still under construction). The PLTMG predates the LNG terminal and is fed by PGN pipeline gas, not by the LNG terminal's own regasified output.

fuel_basis: FLNG standard design runs on produced/feed gas and BOG through its own gas turbines (LM6000PF+, LM2500, Solar Titan 130); off-grid moored FLNG vessel with no shore power option, so self-generation is structural, not optional.

captive_summary: Zhouji (also called the 'Intercontinental'/洲際 or '7th' LNG receiving terminal) is a proposed CPC Corporation Taiwan import facility in Kaohsiung whose own stated, primary purpose -- per CPC's official press release -- is to back up the saturated Yongan terminal and pipe regasified gas OUT to Talin (大林/Daling) power plant's planned new gas-fired generating units. This is the direction-test case: the terminal exists to fuel an external power station, not to power itself with captive generation. No evidence of on-site captive generation for the terminal itself was found in any source.
confirmed_how: CPC Taiwan's own official news release (cpc.com.tw, Jan 2023) states the Intercontinental receiving station's purpose is to 'serve as backup for Yongan, increase southern Taiwan's gas supply volume and supply security,' and that its location adjacent to Talin/Daling Power Plant enables it to 'supply natural gas needed for [the plant's] planned additional gas-generating units.' Corroborated independently by Liberty Times (自由財經) reporting the same project detail: underground pipelines run directly from the terminal to supply gas to both Talin power plant and the Daling distribution station. No source (CPC's own site, Liberty Times, offshore-technology.com data profile, or JOGMEC technical note) describes any on-site captive power generation for the terminal itself.
